submitted.rationale: Index 27 (Bi 0.09, Cu 0.47, V 0.45) had the highest photocurrent of the three merit measurements: 1.53 uA. It sits in the low-Bi region where Cu:V is roughly 1:1, the Cu-vanadate region.

rejected.reason: The BiVO4-like Bi/V-rich composition gave only 0.9 uA.
The more Cu-rich composition near Cu3V2O8 gave 0.71 uA. Photocurrent drops as Cu increases, which fits the small-gap CuO phases predicted by MEGNet/MACE.

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MEGNet shows mp-23262 gap 2.34 eV (near 2.4 eV photon energy, can absorb) while mp-704645 (0.32 eV) and mp-1692 (0.20 eV) are small-gap Cu-rich phases likely to be poor photoanodes/recombination-prone. Favors the Cu-poor, Bi/V-balanced region (BiVO4-like) of index 3 as the first probe.

Largely uninformative for this candidate: MACE confirms mp-704645 is CuO (on hull, small gap), which argues against very Cu-rich compositions. Index 27 (Cu 0.47, V 0.45, Bi 0.09) targets the Cu-vanadate region (Cu3V2O8/Cu2V2O7-type, ~2 eV gaps) rather than CuO, exploring a different region from index 3.

Against going further Cu-rich. mp-1692 has a small gap (0.4 eV GLLB), which argues against CuO-dominated compositions. Index 57 (Cu 0.61, V 0.32, Bi 0.08) stays on the Cu-vanadate line near Cu3V2O8 stoichiometry. That is where the best merit so far was measured (idx 27, 1.53 uA vs 0.9 uA for the BiVO4-like idx 3).
